questions.statement: Which sentence uses the second conditional correctly?
questions.context: Conditionals type 2, San Juan, grado 11, W14.

options.text: If I lived closer to San Juan, I would walk to school every day.
options.feedback: Correct. The second conditional expresses an unreal present hypothesis: past simple plus 'would' plus infinitive.

options.text: If I will live closer to San Juan, I would walk to school every day.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The 'if' clause does not take 'will'; in the second conditional it takes the past simple.

options.text: If I had lived closer to San Juan, I would walk to school every day.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Had lived' belongs to the third conditional, which refers to the past rather than the present.

options.text: If I live closer to San Juan, I would walk to school every day.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The present simple in the 'if' clause belongs to the first conditional, not to a present hypothesis of the second conditional.

questions.explanation:
El condicional tipo dos habla del presente con una condicion irreal. Su estructura es pasado simple en la clausula de 'if' y 'would' mas infinitivo en la principal, y casi siempre se usa con 'were' en lugar de 'was' con los sujetos de primera y tercera persona.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'If I ____ (be) taller, I would play basketball professionally.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 2 with were, Ponce, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Was' is possible in informal speech, but in the second conditional the formal, expected form is 'were'.
Incorrect. 'Am' is present tense and does not fit the unreal hypothesis of the second conditional.
Correct. In the second conditional, the verb 'to be' takes the form 'were' with any subject, even with 'I'.
Incorrect. 'Will be' is a future form and does not fit the present hypothesis of the second conditional.

questions.explanation:
El uso de 'were' en lugar de 'was' en el condicional tipo dos es un rasgo distintivo de la lengua escrita formal. Se aplica con 'I', 'he', 'she' e 'it', aunque en el habla cotidiana se usa 'was' con la misma frecuencia.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'If she ____ (study) harder last year, she would have passed the exam.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 3, Carolina, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Studied' is past simple and would belong to the second conditional, not to a past hypothesis.
Correct. The third conditional expresses a past hypothesis: 'had' plus participle in the 'if' clause.
Incorrect. 'Has' is present perfect and does not fit a past action that was carried out.
Incorrect. 'Would study' is the result of a conditional, not the condition, so it is in the wrong place.

questions.explanation:
El condicional tipo tres se refiere a acciones pasadas que no ocurrieron. Su estructura es 'had' mas participio en la clausula de 'if' y 'would have' mas participio en la principal, y sirve para expresar disputas y reproches sobre decisiones pasadas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'If we ____ (have) more free time, we would travel more often.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 2 with the verb to have, Bayamon, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Have' is present tense and belongs to the first conditional, which expresses a real, possible condition.
Incorrect. 'Will have' is future and does not fit the unreal hypothesis of the second conditional.
Incorrect. 'Would have' is the result of the third conditional and goes in the main clause, not in the 'if' clause.
Correct. 'Had' is the past of 'to have' and expresses the present hypothesis of the second conditional.

questions.explanation:
En el condicional tipo dos el pasado simple se usa con cualquier verbo, y en 'to have' ese pasado es 'had'. La confusion aparece porque 'had' tambien figura en el tipo tres, pero alli siempre va seguido de un participio.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'If I ____ (know) the answer, I would have told you yesterday.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 3 in regrets, Arecibo, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Knew' is past simple and belongs to the second conditional, which refers to the present.
Incorrect. 'Have known' is present perfect and does not express an unfulfilled past hypothesis.
Incorrect. 'Would know' is the result of a conditional, not the condition of the sentence.
Correct. 'Had known' is the past perfect and expresses the past hypothesis of the third conditional.

questions.explanation:
El tipo tres tiene una sola diferencia formal con el tipo dos: 'had' mas participio en lugar de pasado simple. Todo lo demas, incluido 'would have' mas participio en la principal, permanece igual.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence mixes the two conditional types correctly?
questions.context: Conditionals type 2 and 3 comparison, Humacao, grado 11, W14.

options.text: If I had studied medicine, I would have worked in a hospital now.
options.feedback: Incorrect. With both clauses in the third conditional, the sentence sounds redundant and does not express the change in the present situation.

options.text: If I had studied medicine, I would be working in a hospital now.
options.feedback: Correct. This is the classic mixed structure: third conditional in the 'if' clause and second conditional in the main clause.

options.text: If I studied medicine, I had been working in a hospital now.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The order is reversed: the second conditional belongs in the main clause and the third conditional in the 'if' clause.

options.text: If I would have studied medicine, I would be working in a hospital now.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Would' never appears in the 'if' clause of a standard conditional.

questions.explanation:
La estructura mixta expresa una situacion pasada que determino el presente: una causa en el condicional tipo tres y una consecuencia en el tipo dos. Se reconoce porque 'if' lleva 'had' mas participio y la principal lleva 'would' mas infinitivo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct form: 'If I ____ rich, I would buy a house near the beach.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 2 with the verb to be, Aguadilla, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Correct. 'Were' is the second conditional form with 'I' and expresses an unreal present hypothesis.
Incorrect. 'Am' is a real present and belongs to the zero or first conditional, depending on the rest of the sentence.
Incorrect. 'Will be' is future and does not fit the unreal present hypothesis of the second conditional.
Incorrect. 'Had been' belongs to the third conditional, which refers to a past hypothesis.

questions.explanation:
En el condicional tipo dos el verbo 'to be' es 'were' con cualquier sujeto, y esa uniformidad es una de las marcas mas reconocibles de este tipo. 'Was' se acepta en el habla, pero 'were' es la forma que se espera por escrito.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'We are sorry; we ____ (not / break) the vase if we had been more careful.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 3 with regrets and apologies, Guayanilla, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Incorrect. After 'would have', the verb takes the participle 'broken', not the base form 'break'.
Incorrect. It mixes the past simple with the irregular past, and the sentence does not form a conditional.
Correct. 'Wouldn't have' plus participle expresses regret about a past action that did not happen.
Incorrect. 'Don't have' is present tense and does not fit a past hypothesis of the third conditional.

questions.explanation:
El arrepentimiento se expresa con 'would have' mas participio en positivo o negativo. La estructura es siempre la misma y el participio es obligatorio, incluso cuando el verbo es irregular como 'to break'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct?
questions.context: Conditionals type 2 in unreal situations, Trujillo Alto, grado 11, W14.

options.text: If I will be you, I would talk to the principal.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Will be' is future and does not fit the unreal hypothesis of this set phrase.

options.text: If I am you, I would talk to the principal.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Am' is a real present, and the set phrase requires 'were' to mark the hypothesis.

options.text: If I were you, I would talk to the principal.
options.feedback: Correct. 'If I were you' is a second conditional set phrase used to give advice based on an unreal hypothesis.

options.text: If I had been you, I would talk to the principal.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Had been' is third conditional and would place the hypothesis in the past, which is not the meaning of the sentence.

questions.explanation:
'If I were you' es una de las estructuras mas frecuentes del condicional tipo dos. Se usa para dar consejo suponiendo una situacion hipotetica, y por eso casi siempre aparece seguida de 'I would' mas infinitivo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'If she ____ (tell) me the truth earlier, everything would have been different.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 3 with the verb to tell, Barceloneta, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Correct. 'Had told' is the past perfect and expresses the past hypothesis of the third conditional.
Incorrect. 'Would have told' is the consequence and belongs in the main clause, not in the 'if' clause.
Incorrect. 'Told' is past simple and belongs to the second conditional, which refers to the present.
Incorrect. 'Has told' is present perfect and does not fit a past hypothesis that never happened.

questions.explanation:
Los verbos de accion del condicional tipo tres siguen siempre el patron 'had' mas participio. Si la frase ya contiene 'would have' en la principal, la clausula de 'if' no puede repetir esa estructura porque las dos partes son distintas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question is correct?
questions.context: Conditionals type 2 with questions, Maunabo, grado 11, W14.

options.text: Where you would live if you would win the lottery?
options.feedback: Incorrect. Question word order requires 'where' to open the sentence, and the 'if' clause cannot take 'would'.

options.text: Where do you would live if you won the lottery?
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Do' cannot come before 'would', because both are auxiliary verbs.

options.text: Where would you live if you will win the lottery?
options.feedback: Incorrect. The 'if' clause does not take 'will'; in a second conditional it uses the past simple.

options.text: Where would you live if you won the lottery?
options.feedback: Correct. 'Would' opens the second conditional question, and the 'if' clause uses the past simple.

questions.explanation:
En las preguntas de condicional tipo dos el 'would' se coloca delante del sujeto, igual que en cualquier otra oracion interrogativa. La clausula de 'if' mantiene el pasado simple y nunca recibe un auxiliar.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the difference between the second and the third conditional?
questions.context: Conditionals type 2 versus type 3, Yauco, grado 11, W14.

options.text: The second is for questions and the third for statements.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Both types appear equally in questions and statements; word order is not what distinguishes them.

options.text: The second refers to an unreal present and the third to an unreal past.
options.feedback: Correct. The second conditional projects a hypothesis onto the present, and the third conditional onto a past action that did not happen.

options.text: The second uses 'would' and the third uses 'will'.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Both use 'would'; what changes is the past simple versus 'had' plus participle in the 'if' clause.

options.text: The second is formal and the third is informal.
options.feedback: Incorrect. There is no difference in register: both are formal structures typical of written and academic language.

questions.explanation:
La distincion es temporal, no de registro ni de estructura sintactica. El tipo dos razona sobre el presente con pasado simple y el tipo tres sobre el pasado con 'had' mas participio, y en ambos casos la principal lleva 'would'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'If I ____ (write) the email sooner, you would have received it yesterday.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 3 with the verb to write, Cayey, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Would have written' is the hypothetical consequence and goes in the main clause.
Correct. 'Had written' expresses the hypothetical past action, and the irregular participle is required in the third conditional.
Incorrect. 'Wrote' is past simple and belongs to the second conditional.
Incorrect. 'Have written' is present perfect and does not express an unfulfilled past hypothesis.

questions.explanation:
El condicional tipo tres conserva la misma irregularidad de los verbos que el presente y el pasado. 'To write' da 'wrote' en pasado simple y 'written' en participio, y el tipo tres siempre exige la segunda forma.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct form: 'If you ____ (be) me, you would apologise right away.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 2 with second person advice, San Sebastian, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Are' is a real present and belongs to the zero or first conditional, not to a hypothesis.
Incorrect. 'Will be' is future and does not express the unreal hypothesis of the second conditional.
Incorrect. 'Had been' is third conditional and would place the hypothesis in a distant past that the sentence does not mention.
Correct. With 'you', 'were' is the second conditional form and keeps the form uniform throughout this conditional type.

questions.explanation:
El condicional tipo dos tiene una sola forma del pasado de 'to be', y esa forma es 'were' con todos los sujetos. Esa uniformidad es precisamente lo que distingue al tipo dos del tipo tres, donde 'to be' da 'had been'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'She would have apologised ____ you had explained the situation.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 3 with unless, Camuy, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Unless' means 'si no' (if not), so it would completely change the meaning of the hypothetical condition.
Incorrect. 'Although' introduces a concession, not a condition, so it does not form a conditional.
Correct. 'If' introduces the past hypothesis, and the main clause with 'would have' plus participle completes the third conditional.
Incorrect. 'Because' introduces a real present or past cause, not the hypothesis the third conditional requires.

questions.explanation:
El condicional tipo tres se construye con 'if' y nunca con 'unless' cuando se quiere expresar una hipotesis. 'Unless' es posible, pero entonces cambia a una condicion real: 'she would have apologised unless you had explained' ya no es una hipotesis.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question is grammatically correct in the second conditional?
questions.context: Conditionals type 2 with professional goals, Luquillo, grado 11, W14.

options.text: If she studied architecture, she would work in her hometown.
options.feedback: Correct. Both parts follow the second conditional: past simple in the 'if' clause and 'would' plus infinitive in the main clause.

options.text: If she will study architecture, she would work in her hometown.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Will' does not appear in the 'if' clause of a second conditional.

options.text: If she studies architecture, she would work in her hometown.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The present simple in the 'if' clause belongs to the first conditional, which is real, not hypothetical.

options.text: If she had studied architecture, she would have worked in her hometown.
options.feedback: Incorrect. With both parts in the third conditional, the sentence sounds like regret, not a hypothesis about the present.

questions.explanation:
El condicional tipo dos se emplea para hablar de planes, metas y situaciones que serian realidad bajo una condicion falsa. El pasado simple en 'if' es la senal inequivoca de que se trata de una hipotesis presente y no de una condicion real.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'If you had studied last night, you ____ (pass) the test easily.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 3 with past obligations, Toa Baja, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Correct. 'Would have' plus participle is the hypothetical consequence of the third conditional.
Incorrect. 'Would pass' is the second conditional consequence and does not match a past perfect clause.
Incorrect. 'Will have' is future perfect and does not fit a past hypothesis.
Incorrect. After 'would have', the verb takes the participle 'passed', never the gerund.

questions.explanation:
El condicional tipo tres exige siempre 'would have' mas participio en la principal. La forma 'would' mas infinitivo corresponde al tipo dos, y combinar las dos estructuras produce una frase ajena a los condicionales estandar.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Question: 'If you had studied, would you have passed?' Answer: '____'
questions.context: Conditionals type 2 and 3 in short answers, Naguabo, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The short-answer form for the third conditional is 'would have', and the rest of the sentence does not provide the correct auxiliary.
Incorrect. 'Will have' is future perfect and does not answer a question about a past hypothesis.
Incorrect. 'Did' answers a past simple question, not one built with 'would have'.
Correct. The short answer repeats 'would have' from the question, which is the form specific to the third conditional.

questions.explanation:
En una respuesta corta al condicional tipo dos basta 'would', y al tipo tres 'would have'. Como la condicion no se repite, ambas lecturas son posibles y las dos formas se consideran correctas en un examen.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'If he ____ (have) a car, he would not spend so much on taxis.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 2 with the verb to have, Hatillo, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Will have' is future and does not fit the unreal hypothesis the sentence sets up.
Correct. 'Had' is the past of 'to have' and forms the present hypothesis of the second conditional.
Incorrect. 'Has' is present tense and forms a first conditional with a real condition.
Incorrect. 'Had had' belongs to the third conditional with 'to have', not to the second conditional, which only needs the past simple.

questions.explanation:
El tipo dos pide el pasado simple de cualquier verbo, y en 'to have' ese pasado es 'had'. La forma 'had had' solo aparece en el tipo tres, y ese tipo exigiria ademas 'would have' en la oracion principal.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'If we ____ (go) to Ponce last year, we would have visited the museum.'
questions.context: Conditionals type 3 with the verb to go, Yabucoa, grado 11, W14.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Would have gone' is the hypothetical consequence and goes in the main clause.
Incorrect. 'Went' is past simple and belongs to the second conditional, which refers to the present.
Correct. 'Had gone' is past perfect and forms the past hypothesis of the third conditional.
Incorrect. 'Have gone' is present perfect and does not express an unfulfilled past hypothesis.

questions.explanation:
El participio de 'to go' es 'gone', y el condicional tipo tres lo exige siempre. Igual que en los demas verbos irregulares, la forma del pasado simple 'went' no puede aparecer en la clausula de 'if' de un tipo tres.
